peer_results.rationale: BAC candidates discuss the composition of market-based portfolio VaR and define issuer credit risk, but do not disclose the specific adjustment of removing CVA credit risk components from VaR due to widening spreads as described in the target disclosure. BAC explicitly excludes CVA from its total market-based portfolio VaR by definition (bacl_2024_7_P412_S001) rather than describing a dynamic removal due to spread widening.

Citi's candidate disclosures define the components of the credit portfolio (including CVA and CVA hedges) or the scope of IRE analysis, but do not contain the specific narrative about removing the credit risk component of CVA from Credit Portfolio VaR due to widened credit spreads. Citi's credit portfolio explicitly includes CVA (c_2024_7_P541_S001), contrasting with JPM's removal of this specific component from the VaR measure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit and Funding Spread Sensitivity on Derivatives and Liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Sensitivity to a one basis point increase in credit and funding spreads on derivatives resulted in a $2 million loss in 2024 and 2023, while sensitivity to own credit spreads on elected fair value financial liabilities resulted in gains of $43 million and $42 million respectively, subject to liquidity and hedge performance factors.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS disclose the treatment of Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) and credit spreads within their VaR or sensitivity frameworks. JPM specifically removed the credit risk component of CVA from its Credit Portfolio VaR due to widened credit spreads, noting this exposure is now in a sensitivity table. GS explicitly states that its VaR excludes the impact of changes in counterparty credit spreads (CVA) and details a separate sensitivity analysis for these spreads, which resulted in a $2 million loss sensitivity for derivatives in both 2024 and 2023. While JPM removed the component for model governance consistency due to spread levels, GS maintains an exclusion in VaR but reports the sensitivity separately.

sentences.text: (b)In line with the Firm's internal model governance, the credit risk component of CVA related to certain counterparties was removed from Credit Portfolio VaR due to the widening of the credit spreads for those counterparties to elevated levels.
The related hedges were also removed to maintain consistency.

VaR excludes the impact of changes in counterparty credit spreads, our own credit spreads and unsecured funding spreads on derivatives, as well as changes in our own credit spreads (debt valuation adjustment) on financial liabilities for which the fair value option was elected.

The estimated sensitivity to a one basis point increase in credit spreads (counterparty and our own) and unsecured funding spreads on derivatives (including hedges) was a loss of $2 million as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

peer_results.rationale: MS candidates discuss the scope of the VaR model including credit spread risk generally, and a sensitivity measure for the company's own credit spread on borrowings. They do not address the specific treatment of counterparty CVA credit risk components within Credit Portfolio VaR or the adjustment to remove them due to spread widening.
